extracted.intended_audience: student reporters and newspaper journalists (news writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for newspapermen on composing death/obituary pieces and on reporting political news and elections, including forecasts, election-day coverage, and return/result stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obituary: career and public service summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the decedent's career, length of service, positions held, notable achievements, patents or inventions, and record of performance (e.g., "During his 35 years of service... there was probably no man in the department who was better known or who was better liked...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specifics (years, stations, roles, records such as accidents or lack thereof), highlight practical skills and contributions to the institution, and note recognition by supervisors. Examples in the text include detailed service history of a fire department engineer and Colonel Nelson's editorial activity until a month before death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obituary: personal background and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide birth information, early life, education, apprenticeships or training, and migration or family background (e.g., "Mr White was born at Amherst, October 11, 1842... received his early education... his first employment was in the United States armory...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace formative experiences that explain later work; include places, ages, institutions, and formative employers or mentors to give readers context for the subject's accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obituary: family, survivors, memberships, and community ties
rubrics_metrics.description: List surviving relatives or lack thereof, social/ fraternal/ professional memberships, and community roles (e.g., "He was a member of De Soto lodge of Odd Fellows and of the Firemen's aid association... he leaves no near relatives, but Arthur Green... is expected... to take charge of the funeral.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention clubs, lodges, religious affiliations, charitable activities, and notable friendships or patrons; indicate who will take charge of funeral arrangements when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obituary: funeral arrangements and burial
rubrics_metrics.description: State date/time/place of funeral services, officiating clergy, and place of burial (e.g., "The funeral will be held to-morrow afternoon at Washburn's chapel. Rev Dr Frank W. Merrick of Faith church will officiate. The burial will be in the Springfield cemetery.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear, actionable details so readers can attend or send condolences; include chapel/chapelkeeper, officiant, and cemetery information when known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obituary: human-interest detail and exemplifying anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include anecdotes, personal traits, memorable stories, acts of charity, or emblematic incidents that illustrate character (e.g., Bacigalupo's motto to prevent Italians being buried in Potter's Field; driving the second coach in Gen. Grant's funeral; free funerals and paying coal bills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid specifics to convey the person's social role and moral character; balance laudatory anecdotes with factual reporting. Such details provide local color and explain why the person mattered to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obituary: cause and circumstances of death; last days and quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report cause of death, recent illness or hospital information, dates of decline, and notable last remarks if relevant (e.g., "Mr White was taken ill last May... he remained constantly until his death yesterday." and Colonel Nelson's quoted reflection: "The Lord has been far better to me than I deserve...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be factual about cause and timeline; include direct quotes when they illuminate the subject's state of mind or legacy. Note whether medical details were disclosed and avoid speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling political news vs. elections
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat party conventions, campaign meetings, political speeches, interviews with candidates and party managers like similar material in other fields; election coverage requires different handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that elections demand special forms of story (analysis, day-of reporting, results) and different emphases (timeliness, summarization, forecasting), as outlined in the subsequent election-specific rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three common kinds of election stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Three common kinds of election stories are: (1) an analysis of political conditions preceding an election with or without a forecast of the result, (2) a description of election day conditions and events, (3) the results of the election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate kind for the assignment: background/forecast pieces require analytic evidence; election-day stories focus on conditions and process; result stories synthesize outcomes and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and partisan presentation in political news
rubrics_metrics.description: Although some newspapers treat political news with partisan bias, there is a growing tendency to present both sides fairly in news columns and to confine partisanship to editorials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for fair presentation of opposing views in news reporting; reserve overt advocacy and partisan judgment for the editorial pages. Balance direct statements from both camps where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election return stories: essential summary elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Election return stories consist largely of summaries of the most important results of the election, such as: (1) the candidates elected and defeated, (2) the majority or plurality of the successful candidates, (3) the effect of the election on the political complexion of legislative bodies, (4) causes of victory and defeat, (5) statements by candidates and party managers in regard to the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize results around these elements: list winners/losers and margins, explain shifts in control or balance, analyze causes (local issues, defections), and include official or notable reactions and statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political forecast writing: basis and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecasts should be based on informed estimates and canvassing (e.g., "Estimates as to the relative strength of the three leading political parties are at variance, but some of the best informed politicians are of the opinion that the alignment this year will be vastly different..."). Use check lists, canvasses of counties, comparisons with prior years, and identify likely defections and issue impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support predictions with concrete data (canvasses, town checklists, historical vote patterns, percentage estimates). Discuss plausible vote shifts, effects of third parties or issues (e.g., prohibition), and note where enthusiasm or turnout appear weak or strong. Present competing party claims but weigh them against empirical indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election-day reporting: what to cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Report election-day conditions such as weather, ballot usability, voter turnout patterns and timing (e.g., early rush, percentage in by noon/4pm), speed of voting per voter, delays or lulls, sample-ballot efforts, training/instruction for voters, and anti-fraud/watchers' activity (e.g., Honest Ballot Association squads, challenges and arrests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete timing and percentage figures where available (e.g., "By noon 65 per cent. of the total vote was in..."). Note logistical issues with new ballots, use of sample ballots near polls, presence and actions of watchers, and any extraordinary occurrences that affect voting flow or legitimacy.
